title: Change over a machine's fixture plate against its locators
instruction: Change the machine over to the next job. Put the fixture plate now on the machine table into the empty orange rack bay, then put the next job's plate on the machine table and push it home against both dark locating blocks and the end stop, square. The next job's plate is the staged plate long enough to bear on both locating blocks; the shorter one is for another machine.
context: In a quick changeover (SMED), the next job's fixture plate is staged beside the machine while it runs; at the change the setter racks the old plate and pushes the new one against the machine's fixed locators, which set its position without measuring, so the plate must sit home against every locator. Unlike TK-82VLT8, which copies block positions onto a fixture within 8 mm, and a tote swap in a lane, the new plate must be pushed against a fixed datum of two blocks and a stop to within 2.5 mm and 2 degrees, and the right plate is chosen by whether its length spans the locator pitch, not by colour. Unlike TK-NCPNT9 (clamp a blank against stops with a cam), whole fixture plates are exchanged and the right one is chosen by whether it spans the locators. Done by: machine setters and operators (O*NET 51-4081.00, 51-4035.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Plates: aluminium fixture plates 8 cm deep (x) and 2.5 cm thick, lengths along y 12 cm (current job, 450 g), 10 cm (next job, 380 g) and 7 cm (another machine, 270 g). Machine table: a fixed steel slab 11 x 15 x 1 cm centred at x 34, y 19. On it: two fixed dark locating blocks 1.2 x 1.2 x 1 cm with their near faces at x 38, centred at y 14.2 and 21.8, and a fixed dark end stop 3 x 1.2 x 1 cm with its left face at y 13, centred at x 34. The current plate sits on the slab against both blocks and the stop, centred at x 34, y 19. Rack bay: a fixed orange shelf 10 x 15 x 1 cm centred at x 34, y 42 with two orange end walls (6 x 0.6 x 1.5 cm) on it, 12.8 cm apart inside. Staging mat: a fixed black mat 11 x 23 cm, 2 mm thick, centred at x 17, y 28.5, with the 10 cm plate centred at y 23 and the 7 cm plate at y 36.
scoring: From a top photo and a ruler, with the grippers open. In order, each step needing the ones before: 0.25 the current plate is off the machine table (centre outside the slab); 0.5 it rests flat on the rack shelf between the end walls (centre within 1.5 cm across and 6 mm along the bay, square within 8 degrees); 0.75 the next job's plate rests flat on the machine table; 1.0 it is seated: its far edge within 2.5 mm of both locating blocks and its right edge within 2.5 mm of the end stop, measured square to the plate's edges, and square within 2 degrees. The short plate on the machine table caps the score at 0.5. Success: 1.0, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Seat the 12 cm plate back against the blocks and the stop, and stand the 10 cm and 7 cm plates back on the staging mat.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The locating pins and stop are fixed blocks, and nothing clamps the plate: it is held by gravity and friction where a real plate is clamped or bolted after seating. Plates are solid boxes, lighter than solid aluminium (as if pocketed), without locating holes; the right plate is told by length.
